extraction.diagnosis: Acute on chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)
extraction.hospital_summary: You came in with shortness of breath and leg swelling from extra fluid. We removed about 4 kg (9 lb) of fluid with IV diuretics. Your discharge weight is 78.2 kg (172 lb).

medications.name: Furosemide (Lasix)
medications.source_quote: Furosemide (Lasix) 40 mg tablet. Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily in the morning. Purpose: removes extra fluid.

medications.name: Spironolactone
medications.purpose:
heart failure; helps the
heart and keeps potassium up.
medications.source_quote:
Spironolactone 25 mg tablet. Take 1/2 tablet (12.5 mg) by mouth once daily. Purpose: heart failure; helps the
heart and keeps potassium up.

medications.name: Metoprolol succinate ER
medications.source_quote:
Metoprolol succinate ER 25 mg tablet. Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily. Dose lowered from 50 mg because
your heart rate was slow. Do not crush or chew.

medications.name: Lisinopril
medications.source_quote: Lisinopril 5 mg tablet. Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily. Purpose: blood pressure and heart protection.

medications.name: Atorvastatin
medications.source_quote: Atorvastatin 40 mg tablet. Take 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime. Purpose: cholesterol.

medications.name: Amlodipine
special_instructions: Replaced by your new heart failure medicines.
medications.source_quote: Amlodipine 10 mg tablet. Stop taking. Replaced by your new heart failure medicines.

medications.name: Ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin)
medications.source_quote:
Ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) and naproxen (Aleve). Do not take. These can make heart failure and kidney function
worse. Use acetaminophen (Tylenol) for pain instead.

medications.name: naproxen (Aleve)
medications.source_quote:
Ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) and naproxen (Aleve). Do not take. These can make heart failure and kidney function
worse. Use acetaminophen (Tylenol) for pain instead.

appointments.time_window: any time between 8:00 AM and 4:00 PM
appointments.purpose:
This checks your kidneys and potassium on the new
medicines.

Blood test (basic metabolic panel): Tuesday 10/20/2026, any time between 8:00 AM and 4:00 PM, Maplewood
Outpatient Lab, Ground floor. No appointment needed. This checks your kidneys and potassium on the new
medicines.

appointments.what_to_bring: your weight log and all your medicine bottles

Cardiology clinic, Dr. Ananya Rao: Thursday 10/22/2026 at 10:30 AM, Heart and Vascular Center, 2nd floor. Bring
your weight log and all your medicine bottles.
Primary care, Dr. James Whitfield: within 2 weeks. Call (203) 555-0142 to schedule.

warnings.source_quote:
Call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room if: you have chest pain or pressure; severe shortness of breath at
rest; you faint or pass out; you cough up pink, frothy mucus.

instructions.text:
Weigh yourself every morning after you urinate and before breakfast, wearing similar clothing. Write the number
down and bring the log to your appointments.
instructions.source_quote:
Weigh yourself every morning after you urinate and before breakfast, wearing similar clothing. Write the number
down and bring the log to your appointments.

instructions.text: Limit all fluids to 2 liters (about 8 cups) per day.
instructions.source_quote: Limit all fluids to 2 liters (about 8 cups) per day.

instructions.text: Eat a low-salt diet: less than 2,000 mg of sodium per day.
instructions.source_quote: Eat a low-salt diet: less than 2,000 mg of sodium per day.

instructions.source_quote: Walk for 10 to 15 minutes, 2 to 3 times a day.

explanation.summary: You were in the hospital because your heart failure got worse and your body held onto too much fluid, causing shortness of breath and leg swelling. Doctors gave you IV water pills to remove about 4 kg (9 lb) of extra fluid. When you left the hospital, you weighed 78.2 kg (172 lb).

m1.what_for: It removes extra fluid from your body.
m1.how_to_take: Take 1 tablet (40 mg) by mouth once a day in the morning.

m2.what_for: It helps your heart with heart failure and helps keep your potassium level up.
m2.how_to_take: Take half a tablet (12.5 mg) by mouth once a day.

m3.how_to_take: Take 1 tablet (25 mg) by mouth once a day. Your dose was lowered from 50 mg because your heart rate was slow.
tips: Do not crush or chew the tablet.

m4.what_for: It helps control your blood pressure and protects your heart.
m4.how_to_take: Take 1 tablet (5 mg) by mouth once a day.

m5.how_to_take: Take 1 tablet (40 mg) by mouth at bedtime.

m6.how_to_take: Stop taking this medicine (10 mg). It has been replaced by your new heart failure medicines.
tips: This medicine was replaced by your new heart failure medicines.

m7.how_to_take: Do not take this medicine anymore.

m8.how_to_take: Do not take this medicine anymore.

signs: Your weight goes up more than 2 pounds in one day, or 5 pounds in one week.
Your legs, ankles, or belly swell more.
You feel dizzy or light-headed when you stand up.
You need more pillows to breathe at night.

w2.who_to_call: Call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room.
signs: You have chest pain or pressure.
You have severe shortness of breath while resting.
You cough up pink, frothy mucus.

i1.text: Weigh yourself every morning after you use the bathroom and before breakfast, wearing similar clothing each time. Write down your weight and bring this log to your appointments.

i2.text: Limit all the fluids you drink to 2 liters (about 8 cups) each day.

i3.text: Eat a low-salt diet. Have less than 2,000 mg of sodium (salt) each day.

i4.text: Walk for 10 to 15 minutes, 2 to 3 times a day.

i5.text: Do not lift anything heavier than 10 pounds for 2 weeks.

a1.text: Get a blood test (basic metabolic panel) on October 20, 2026, any time between 8:00 AM and 4:00 PM, at Maplewood Outpatient Lab, Ground floor. This checks your kidneys and potassium on your new medicines.

a2.text: See Dr. Ananya Rao at the Cardiology clinic on October 22, 2026, at 10:30 AM, at the Heart and Vascular Center, 2nd floor. Bring your weight log and all your medicine bottles.

a3.text: Call Dr. James Whitfield's office within 2 weeks to schedule a primary care visit. The phone number is (203) 555-0142.

questions.question: What strength and dose of acetaminophen (Tylenol) should I use for pain, how often can I take it, and what is the most I should take in a day?
questions.reason: The instructions say to use acetaminophen for pain instead, but they don't say the dose, how often to take it, or the daily limit.

labels.summary: Why you were in the hospital
labels.emergency: Call 911 or go to the emergency room
labels.times_note: Clock times are suggestions. Your papers say how often (for example, twice daily); Going Home spreads the doses across the day. Keep the spacing and move them to fit your day, or ask your pharmacist.
labels.first_day_note: On the day you leave the hospital, ask the nurse which of today's doses were already given, so none are doubled.
